// Part: room: east hall bath. Interior box x63..68, y11..16, z54..60 (plan: the hall bath for the east rooms and the wing).
// Layout: the tub is the focal piece on the south wall, facing the north door; the vanity (basin on a quartz counter)
// is on the west wall by the west doorway; linen barrels sit on the east wall by the window; a bath mat lies in front
// of the tub. One hanging lantern from the ceiling lights the room. Only air is written (layers() never replaces).
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

const ORIGIN = [63, 11, 54]; // top-left interior cell (x63, z54); rows run along +x, successive rows along +z

const LEGEND = {
  Q: "smooth_quartz", // counter block
  C: "cauldron", // basin on the counter
  P: "flower_pot", // vanity pot
  W: ["water_cauldron", { level: "3" }], // the tub
  M: "white_carpet", // bath mat
  B: "barrel", // linen barrels
  K: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom", shape: "straight" }], // stool, seat faces the vanity
  H: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // ceiling lantern
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }], // standing lantern on the floor by the tub
};

// stand row y11: floor furniture (rows z54..z60, columns x63..x68; no spaces, one character per cell)
const FLOOR = [
  "QK...B", // z54: vanity counter by the north-west corner, linen barrel by the east wall
  "QK...B", // z55: counter, stool, barrel
  "......", // z56: west door lane (x63) stays clear
  "......", // z57
  "......", // z58: window side (x68) stays clear
  ".MMMML", // z59: bath mat in front of the tub, lantern at the east end
  ".WWWW.", // z60: the tub along the south wall
];

// counter top row y12
const TOP = [
  "C.....", // z54: basin on the counter
  "P.....", // z55: flower pot on the counter
];

// ceiling row y16
const CEILING = [
  "......",
  "......",
  "..H...", // z56: hanging lantern over the room's centre, clear of both doorways
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, ORIGIN, LEGEND, [FLOOR]);
  layers(g, [63, 12, 54], LEGEND, [TOP]);
  layers(g, [63, 16, 54], LEGEND, [CEILING]);
}

input.summary:
room: east hall bath (parts/room-23.mjs) now writes nothing: its 18 writes all targeted cells the mansion shell had filled with air, and runParts refuses writes into any cell an earlier part wrote, air included.
Its line in make.sh shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE, and make.sh still writes build.nbt. The layout (floor furniture, counter top, ceiling lantern) is kept as data in the file, with a comment.
The part is not furnished: the room has no free cells until shell.mjs stops filling the interior with air. All blocks used are on palette.json.
left: Room is empty: shell.mjs:27 fills x27..68 z43..60 y4..16 with air (`fill([x0+1,3,z0+1],[x1-1,17,z1-1],"air")`), so all 252 cells of this room (x63..68 y11..16 z54..60) are owned by the shell. The 18 writes were refused and have been removed from build(); the layout constants are kept. Fix belongs in shell.mjs (leave the room interior unowned, or let furnishing parts write into shell air) and then restore the three layers() calls (floor at y11, counter top at y12, ceiling lantern at y16).

Room-23's blocks are on palette; the OFF-PALETTE lines in make.sh are from roof.json (tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, tuff_brick_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_slab, polished_deepslate_slab, polished_deepslate_stairs, stone_brick_slab). Not this part; fix roof.json.
parts/room-23.mjs-E is a stray copy in the parts directory. It is untouched and not loaded by build.mjs.

waste.what: Traced each refused cell to its owner by hand: the REFUSED line gives coordinates but no owning part, so I read runParts' write() and shell.mjs to find the air fill.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls, plus one make.sh run with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and a node check of all 252 room cells
waste.tool: runParts' refusal line should name the owning part and the cell's owner (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell'), and `mcd plan` should list locked cells per room box, so a designer sees the room is closed before writing 18 blocks.

waste.what: Off-palette checking is blind to refused writes: write() returns before the palette check, so an off-palette block in a locked cell is never reported. I checked the eight block ids by hand with a node one-liner against palette.json.
waste.tool: `$MCD blocks --check` over the part's ids, or a palette pass that runs before the lock check.

waste.what: Deciding what to do with 18 refused writes meant working out, cell by cell, whether any cell in the room could take them. No tool showed free cells in the box, so I had to prove it was all owned.
waste.cost: 3 layers() calls, 18 refused writes, and 3 full make.sh rebuilds to check one part
waste.tool: A `layers()` or `mcd plan` dry run that reports, per cell, free or locked (and by which part), so the designer can move writes instead of deleting them and never needs a full rebuild to test one part.
